en: Now, as I mentioned in the last lecture,
this course does not focus on a specific
programming paradigm.
You can follow along no matter if you wanna
do functional, object-oriented, or
procedural programming or anything else.
Things like naming things correctly and
writing good functions will always apply. Of
course, you still might have
paradigm-specific patterns, principles, and
conventions, which you should still take
into account even after finishing this
course. So if the style you're using or also
the programming language you're using has
extra style guides or rules, you should of
course still respect these
even if that's not covered in this course
because this course focuses on general
universal clean code rules. So of course,
don't abandon other rules or concepts which
might apply to the style you are using.
Nonetheless, the core principles and rules
which are covered in this course will always
apply
no matter which style or programming
language you're using. It's always about
using good readable and meaningful names.
It's always about having slim and concise
functions which are easy to read. And of
course, you always want an understandable
code flow and no deeply nested if
statements. So this will all always apply,
and therefore the concepts taught in this
course will always apply.
